dicas.texto: Você sabe que 8/8 representa o inteiro completo, chegando até o final da reta. Se você quer uma fração equivalente que também represente o inteiro completo, onde na reta numérica o ponto deve estar?
Após dividir a reta em 5 partes, marque o ponto que representa o valor total, ou seja, o ponto que está exatamente alinhado com o final da reta (o número 1).
Para representar o inteiro completo usando quintos, você precisa contar todas as 5 partes. Qual é o numerador que indica que você pegou todas as 5 partes de 5?
Se você tem 5 partes no total e quer chegar ao mesmo valor de 8/8 (que é 1), você deve selecionar a marcação que representa 5 de 5. Que número você deve colocar no campo do numerador?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Eight eighths equals how many fifths?"; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

When every part of the line is included, the point is at the endpoint of the interval.
Move to the endpoint that represents one complete whole.

misconceptions.description: O aluno tenta manter a diferença constante entre numerador e denominador (8-8=0, logo X-5=0, X=5).
misconceptions.feedback: You focused on the difference between the numerator and denominator instead of the point represented on the line. Equivalent fractions are identified by their location, and 8/8 is at the whole.

nodes.description: Divide Line 2 into equal parts for fifths, then confirm the denominator.
nodes.instruction: Divide Line 2 into equal parts for fifths, then confirm the denominator.

hints.message: The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole.
Read the unit named in the question and use that number for the equal divisions.
The new fraction must have the denominator that matches the word fifths.
Enter the number of equal sections named by fifths and confirm the division.

misconceptions.description: O aluno confunde o valor do denominador com o valor da fração unitária na reta.
misconceptions.feedback: The field asks for the number of equal divisions, not a unit fraction. Enter only the count of parts.

misconceptions.description: O aluno tenta realizar uma operação aritmética simples entre os números visíveis em vez de buscar equivalência.
misconceptions.feedback: You combined visible numbers instead of using the requested unit. The line must be divided according to the number of parts in fifths.

misconceptions.description: O aluno aplica uma regra genérica de 'metade' sem considerar que a fração original é o inteiro (8/8).
misconceptions.feedback: The task is not asking for half of the denominator. Use the number of equal parts named by fifths.

nodes.description: Mark on Line 2 the point that matches the whole shown on Line 1.
nodes.instruction: Mark on Line 2 the point that matches the whole shown on Line 1.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions point to the same location on a number line.
Use the marked point on Line 1 as the reference, then find the same location on Line 2.
After dividing the line into equal parts, look at the endpoint of the interval from 0 to 1.
Click the final mark of Line 2, where the complete interval ends.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas incluindo o zero como a primeira marca, terminando em uma posição além do inteiro.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted marks instead of intervals and went past the whole. Count the equal spaces from 0 to the endpoint.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator that completes the fraction in fifths.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator that completes the fraction in fifths.

hints.message: The numerator counts how many equal parts are represented.
Use the point marked on Line 2 and count the parts from 0 to that point.
Because the point is at the whole, every part created for the denominator is included.
Enter the same count as the total number of fifth-sized parts in the complete interval.

nodes.description: Select the equality sign between 8/8 and the fraction in fifths.
nodes.instruction: Select the equality sign between 8/8 and the fraction in fifths.

hints.message: Compare the locations of the two fractions rather than comparing their numerators alone.
Use the number lines to decide whether the two fractions represent the same amount.
The two marked points are at the same endpoint of the interval.
Choose the symbol that means both sides have the same value.

nodes.description: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction response.
nodes.instruction: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction response.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that both fractions represent the same point on the number lines.
Review the denominator, marked point, numerator, and comparison sign in order.
Make sure the right-hand fraction shows the numerator that counts all the equal parts in the whole.
When the complete equivalent-fraction statement is displayed, press the Done button.
